hints: Focus on iodide as a reducing agent, it is the strongest reducing halide ion so it reduces sulfuric acid the furthest.
Remember concentrated sulfuric acid with S at +6 can be reduced stepwise to sulfur dioxide, to sulfur, and then even further.
List the oxidation numbers for $\text{SO}_2$, $\text{S}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ and pick the smallest value to finish the logic.
walkthrough:
**Spot the roles: oxidiser and reducer**

Think of this as a redox battle. Iodide, $\text{I}^-$, is a very good reducing agent, so it gives electrons away. Concentrated sulfuric acid is a good oxidising agent, so it takes those electrons and its sulfur is reduced.

Starting oxidation numbers:
$$\text{I in NaI} = -1, \quad \text{S in H}_2\text{SO}_4 = +6$$

**Recall how far sulfuric acid is reduced**

Chloride only gives $\text{HCl}$, bromide gives $\text{SO}_2$, but iodide is strong enough to go further. It produces all three reduction products.

$$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 (+6) \to \text{SO}_2 (+4) \to \text{S} (0) \to \text{H}_2\text{S} (-2)$$

**Find the lowest sulfur oxidation number**

Now assign oxidation numbers to each sulfur-containing reduction product. $\text{SO}_2$ has S at +4, free sulfur $\text{S}$ is 0, and in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, H is +1 so S must be -2.

Lowest value:
$$-2 < 0 < +4 < +6$$

options.A: Correct. Iodide reduces sulfuric acid all the way to hydrogen sulfide, $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, where sulfur is at -2. This is the lowest possible sulfur oxidation state here, lower than $\text{SO}_2$ (+4) and $\text{S}$ (0).
options.B: Not the lowest. Elemental sulfur, $\text{S}$, with oxidation number 0 is indeed formed from iodide, but iodide is strong enough to reduce sulfur even further to $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ at -2.
options.C: Not the lowest. Sulfur dioxide, $\text{SO}_2$, with sulfur at +4 is formed, but this is only the first reduction step. With NaI, reduction continues to S (0) and $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ (-2).
options.D: Incorrect. +6 is the oxidation number of sulfur in the starting concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and in the salt $\text{NaHSO}_4$. The question asks for reduced products, so the value must be lower than +6.
